wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/regmsg.txt: fix(streams): stream_filter_register() replaced any name it was given, and the registry kept a pointer it did not own

`stream_filter_register()` answered `true` for every call. php answers `false`
rather than replacing a registration, so a program that branches on the result —
which is the only reason the function returns one — took the wrong path:

```php
var_dump(stream_filter_register('string.toupper', 'MyFilter'));  // php: false
var_dump(stream_filter_register('my.upper', 'MyFilter'));        // php: true
var_dump(stream_filter_register('my.upper', 'MyFilter'));        // php: false
```
